answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashed reputation bond. Each identity locks collateral and earns one signed attestation from an older member; peers audit a random sample, and any identity proven a duplicate forfeits its bond while its endorsers share the penalty. To pose as many agents, an attacker must fund a separate bond per fake name and grow a distinct chain of guarantors for each, so cost outruns the seats won. Even a small shop trading garden seed, pigment, or cedar must show a unique record first, making a thousand throwaway bots far dearer than one honest trader.
